discrepancies.topic: Injection section shows only the safe query

a.value: 'Without the proper protections in our own code, a bad actor could run malicious code. Consider the following:' followed by the ? placeholder version

b.value: The lecture first builds the query with an f-string, shows the attack, and then says this is 'not how you should ever write SQL code in Python' before switching to ?

discrepancies.note: The notes' code is the protected version. The Persian note says so explicitly and adds an authored, fixture-run demo of the unsafe f-string next to the safe ? version (labelled تألیفی).

discrepancies.topic: 'sanitize and remove any potentially malicious characters'

a.value: 'the library will sanitize and remove any potentially malicious characters'; '? ... validation can be run on username and password'

b.value: 'Any dangerous characters will be escaped for you' (lecture); on the build box cs50 9.5.0 stores and matches an input containing ' and -- literally, nothing is removed (src-sql-box-7)

discrepancies.note: Placeholders bind the value as data (escaping it), they neither delete characters nor validate the value. The Persian note uses 'escape/bind' and keeps 'never trust user input' as the official rule.

discrepancies.topic: 'index by the keys of a list'

a.value: 'Python also allows you to index by the keys of a list' (introducing csv.DictReader)

b.value: csv.DictReader yields one dict per row (keys from the header row); a list is indexed by integers only

discrepancies.note: Persian note: each row is a dictionary whose keys are the column names.

discrepancies.topic: Topic order differs between lecture and notes

a.value: sorted(counts) and sorted(..., key=counts.get, reverse=True) appear in the flat-file section; Race Conditions precedes SQL Injection Attacks

b.value: The lecture demonstrates sorted() at about 1:47:51 (just before Using SQL in Python) and covers SQL injection (about 1:58:00) before race conditions (about 2:06:24)

discrepancies.note: Notes keep the official notes' order; each note links to its own place in the video, so two notes have start times out of order (n01's sorted part and n12).

b.value: HTTP 404 on 2026-10-29; cdn.cs50.net/2025/fall/sections/7/src7.zip and src7/ also 404; only section7.pdf answers 200

discrepancies.note: The Persian section page is built from the transcript only and says the code link was unavailable when checked. Anything Songs-specific is summarised without queries (D57).

discrepancies.topic: Section: 'there aren't different types' of join

a.value: 'this is the only way of using joining. There aren't different types.'

b.value: SQLite supports INNER JOIN (plain JOIN), LEFT [OUTER] JOIN, CROSS JOIN and, since 3.39, RIGHT and FULL OUTER JOIN

discrepancies.note: Persian section page: CS50 Week 7 only needs the plain (inner) JOIN; other kinds exist. Authored note in w07-n08 mentions LEFT JOIN as 'beyond this course'.

discrepancies.topic: Single vs double quotes 'just a styling thing'

a.value: 'the single quote versus the double quotes, it's really just a styling thing'; src-practice-favorites uses UPDATE ... SET title = "How I Met Your Mother"

b.value: In standard SQL single quotes delimit strings and double quotes delimit identifiers; SQLite accepts a double-quoted string only as a legacy fallback when no column has that name (quirks.html#dblquote). On the box, WHERE name = "name" compares the column with itself and matches every row

discrepancies.note: Package rule: string literals always in single quotes. The Favorites guide reproduces nothing from the official UPDATE examples and explains the quoting rule.

discrepancies.topic: Section: joins 'typically a bit slower than nested selects'

a.value: 'joins are typically going to be a bit slower than nested selects, but it does depend on the situation'

b.value: SQLite's query planner may rewrite subqueries and joins; there is no general rule that one form is slower (the speaker also says it depends)

discrepancies.note: Persian page says: choose the form you can read and check; measure with .timer on if speed matters.

discrepancies.topic: Official Songs and Movies hints contain full answer queries

a.value: Each Songs hint block shows the complete query for the corresponding numbered file; the Movies hints show a complete nested query for one numbered file

b.value: Package rule FR-13 / D56: no solution content; the CS50 honesty policy forbids copying solutions

discrepancies.note: Hint sections are link-only in the Persian guides; validate.py forbids the hint query strings anywhere in week-07 (D56).

discrepancies.topic: SQL short (2017) is from the web-development unit of an older CS50

a.value: 'in our videos on web development...'; uses MySQL types (CHAR, VARCHAR, ENUM...) and phpMyAdmin; 'You probably won't do too many joins'

b.value: CS50x 2026 teaches SQL in Week 7, before Flask (Week 9), with sqlite3 in cs50.dev; Movies and Fiftyville rely on joins or nested queries

discrepancies.note: Persian short page flags the MySQL-only parts and maps the SQLite affinities to the lecture's list.

discrepancies.topic: SQL short: CHAR padded with 'null bytes'

a.value: CHAR(10) storing a 2-letter string 'would also store 8 extra-- the equivalent of null bytes'

b.value: SQLite ignores the length in CHAR(n)/VARCHAR(n) (TEXT affinity, no padding); MySQL pads CHAR with spaces, not null bytes, and strips them on retrieval

discrepancies.note: Persian short page states the SQLite behaviour and keeps the short's idea (fixed vs variable width) as MySQL background.

a.value: favorites10.py: comment '# Search for title' above a query that counts a problem

b.value: favorites9.py has the same comment above a GROUP BY language query; neither searches titles

discrepancies.note: Code kept verbatim; the Persian note describes what the query does.

a.value: 'In sqlite, we have five data types': BLOB, INTEGER, NUMERIC ('for numbers that are formatted specially like dates'), REAL, TEXT

b.value: SQLite has five storage classes (NULL, INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB) and five column type affinities (TEXT, NUMERIC, INTEGER, REAL, BLOB); there is no date type, dates are stored as TEXT, REAL or INTEGER

discrepancies.note: Persian note keeps the official list as 'column types (affinities)' and adds a labelled inference about storage classes and dates.

discrepancies.topic: sqlite3 asks to create the file

a.value: 'Upon being prompted, we will agree that we want to create favorites.db by pressing y'

b.value: The stock sqlite3 shell opens or creates the file without asking; the y/n prompt is added by the cs50.dev environment

discrepancies.note: Persian note: in cs50.dev you are asked; elsewhere the file is created (on the first write) without a question.
